Can’t recommend this game to anyone when the developers aren’t capable of simple math. To illustrate this, after playing for an hour, I have a health of about 385 and DPS of 91.7. This is after defeating everything several times. Now you’re left to wait 30-40 minutes MORE for enough respawns. You’re stuck either leaving the game or walking around in this tiny, confined area for that time. It’s so bad it’s funny. There was clearly zero QA to get to this point and all they will want to do is suck money from you. There are so many other games that aren’t nearly as egregious with trying to get you to spend money but this one just feels like an attempt at extortion it’s so thoughtlessly developed. Spend your time elsewhere.

title: A waiting room with a hook
body: Each island has about five minutes of real content, and the game stretches it into a week with respawn timers. You log in, kill a few enemies in 20 seconds, then wait half an hour to do it again — all for stat crumbs so small you can’t even feel them. Progress isn’t slow, it’s geological. Bosses are tuned like you should be three times stronger than the game ever lets you be, unless you pay for VIP to buy back the speed the game took from you in the first place. It’s not that the game is hard. It’s that there’s barely a game here — just timers, grinding, and a shop. Played for days and felt like I’d accomplished nothing. Not fun, not rewarding, not worth the storage space.

title: Frequent crashes, cash grab
body: I rarely write reviews on games in the App Store unless they are utter garbage. This is one of those games. Let me preface this, I played this game for a few hours, I wanted to give it an honest chance and see if it was a good game. Right out the gate killed a few enemies and chopped a few trees. Died for the first time and the game crashed. Opened the game again and died and the game crashed again. Hard to play for more than a few minutes when the game is crashing every few minutes. Again, I wanted to know if the game was worth tolerating all the crashes. It was not. There is not much of a game outside of spending money. 3 minute timers on the first trees and enemies and the timer get longer the deeper you go???? The long timers would make sense if you were making good progress and they actually gave anything good outside of 1 attack or 3 health. The spawn timers in the ad were much better and that version of the game was actually playable. So beware, if you want to actually play the game you have to spend. I didn't spend a dime so I can't tell you how worth it this game is if you spend money on it, but just with the frequent crashes, I'm going to go out on a limb and say not worth it.

title: Has Potential
body: Editing my review to 1 star as the crashing has gotten worse. It’s now impossible to play. This game could be really solid… but there are a few major flaws. First, it randomly freezes requiring you to click your phone off and then on to force close the app and restart. Next, the enhance crystal % is definitely broken. It’ll tell you there’s a 40% chance to enhance but there’s zero chance that’s accurate… I’ve had so many fails in a row at that level it’s statistically impossible for it to be accurate. Finally, there just needs to be more to do… more special events and more activities rather than just walking around the islands every day.

title: Spawn Timer Simulator
body: Honestly the game itself is decent, has some fun mechanics. I see what they’re going for. I can see how it has potential. UNFORTUNATELY… these devs have no clue how to make it a proper game. They’ve put these very dumb spawn timers on all the enemies. And I’m not talking like a minute here or there, literally entire days. Like a 24 hour timer for weak enemies. So now I’m stuck because the big bad enemy I need to kill to get to the next stage is too powerful for me, and the only way to get stronger is to wait out these idiotic 24 hour timers so I can beat the smaller guys again and again and grind to the level needed. So I literally have to close out of the game and wait. What’s even the point of this? All it does is make people not play your game. Isn’t the whole purpose of these kinds of games to keep people engaged? How is this possibly engaging anyone? Game has great potential but horrible execution. It’s too bad really. I’ll have to keep an eye out for a similar copycat game that actually does it right since these devs can’t seem to.

The game immediately falls short the moment you realize it’s designed strictly for pay to play. You have to wait absurdly long monster respawn periods, there is no way to earn VIP points other than purchasing purple crystals that you need for upgrading and you also can’t earn purple crystals. They can only be purchased. So essentially after you have killed everything about three times you have a 22 - 24 hour wait on respawns in order to continue the game play. Then the few monsters remaining are designed as such that you are just barely weaker than and can’t beat them without powering up or so absurdly OP that the difference in strength is almost laughable in such a way that one can only assume it’s to play one one’s desire to overcome thus pushing you to purchase power upgrades. That’s not playing a game. That’s monetized button pushing. I would have been more inclined to pay for the game had it just been presented as a premium game experience with actual RPG fantasy game mechanics instead of this pay to play never making it any further than your last Apple Pay can afford you. title: Game Function
body: Been playing this for maybe about half a year to a year? Gone through the early stages up to now. It’s fun and the actual mechanics of playing are definitely entertaining and engaging. The progression however, is pretty abysmally slow. Especially once you’ve progressed far enough in the soul tree, when you kill something on the regular map(tree, mob, boss), it immediately kills them for as many times as allowed in a day, then you have to wait until the next day to be able to kill them again. This basically puts a hard cap on how much you can progress per day, which makes the game much less interesting. Once you get to evolving weapons, you have to kill a boss to get maybe 1 or 2 of the equipment to drop. The upgrades scale by 100,500,1200,3000 or something like that. So in order to evolve a weapon that I can only get once per day, I’d have to play a ridiculous amount of time that frankly isn’t worth it. And this is across the board for armor and weapons. Money wise the game is pretty sleazy. To get the higher (and only impactful) rewards in the crystal golem event, you actually can’t earn your way to them, without spending in game or real life currency. This is cause of the golem spawn timing, and the set maximum of golems on the map. The mythic souls are tied up behind a $30 purchase and you only get 1 per purchase. Have never bought one, cause the quality-of-life improvements aren’t worth the money frankly. That’s fine and all. The reason I’m probably gonna stop playing is cause the removal of certain unique traits during updates that allowed for grinding. There have been different areas or methods to farm mobs rapidly, (including an infinite cactus spawn that was removed), which honestly was the most fun part of the game. The ability to rapidly grow the character’s power and watch him curbstomp enemies until he couldn’t was part of the thrill of playing. Now with the new update, the ability to progress rapidly is gone, meaning the player is again, forced into the daily spawn constraint of the mobs. All in all, fun game, but because of the repeated removal of the most fun and rewarding parts, it’s lost its appeal.

title: New updates are slowly correcting the balance broken by the overhaul, getting much better
body: Update: the most recent update has opened up a path for F2P to earn rewards after a one time purchase. This is significantly improved over the previous position, and the game, in my opinion, is worth the cost. There are still portions that have not been released and it is still very much a slow grind game, especially in the last islands, but with the introduction of some purchasable items (namely the Crystal jar) it is now slowly possible to grind your way to unlocking the other new weapons and accessories. This will still require a 25$ purchase as there is no possible way currently to spawn sufficient minions to reach the 400 kill count required for the item unlocks without paying, but allowing a single purchase to open the grind again makes this acceptable to me. The new update has also stabilized again and the balance is improving with the new items, I’m optimistic of the outlook, but cannot rate above 4* as there are still multiple portions of the advancement paths and games that are directly tied to required purchases (25-75$) TLDR: new update made game Pay to Play instead of allowing natural progression. Balancing is needed before the game returns to being playable. Prior to the new update, this was a fun time suck. It didn’t require much thought, but it was fun to play and a good way to kill time. The new update introduced new features that may be fun once they’re properly implemented, but the way they were implemented trashed the existing benefits of the game. The introduction of new enemies that have 70% evasion rates and a unmatchable self healing rate, in addition to the complete redo of original equipment has skewed this to a point that as a player from before the update, has, in my opinion created a massive negative impact on the gaming experience. Additionally, restricting entire portions of the Soul Tree behind a 30$ paywall (not a one time fee, but a weekly charge that you then have to sit with and wait for) guarantees that you cannot access entire portions of the gameplay without spending. Additionally, the restructuring of the event (critical rewards are no longer tied to the bosses you defeat during the event, but instead on how many minion you manage to kill before time expires) has completely ruined the event as you will now need to play continuously through the entire 2hr duration of the event, and still will not even progress into the higher tier rewards of the event.
